task.title: Write text in vertical lines
task.shortdesc: You write text in vertical lines by setting writing-mode on an element. The characters of Chinese and Japanese stand upright, one under another, and the lines follow each other from right to left. The vertical text reference lists the properties used here.

context.p: The element names in the examples, such as book and p, are placeholders. Use the names that occur in your XML. The font must have the characters of the text, so declare a font with @font-face, as explains. The standard fonts of PDF have no Chinese, Japanese or Korean characters.

info.p: Set writing-mode to vertical-rl on the root element to write the whole document in vertical lines:

The root element also sets the writing mode of the page, so the page area is laid out in vertical lines too, the first line is at the right edge of the page and the text goes on to the next page when the lines reach the left edge. Any other element can have its own writing mode. The value is inherited, so the elements inside take it.

vertical-lr starts the lines at the left edge. sideways-rl and sideways-lr turn all the characters, Latin or Japanese, a quarter turn, and are for text that reads sideways. A page written in sideways-rl is the horizontal page turned a quarter clockwise, and one in sideways-lr is the horizontal page turned a quarter counterclockwise.

step.cmd: Choose how the characters are turned

info.p: In a vertical line, text-orientation decides what happens to the characters:

ul.li: mixed, the initial value, keeps the characters of Chinese, Japanese and Korean upright and turns a quarter clockwise the characters of the other scripts, so Latin words read from top to bottom.
upright keeps every character upright. A Latin word is then a stack of letters, from top to bottom.

image.alt: Three vertical lines. Each one has two Chinese characters and the Latin word Word. With mixed, the characters are upright and the word is turned a quarter clockwise. With upright, the characters and the four letters of the word are all upright. With sideways, the characters and the word are all turned.

info.p: glyph-orientation-vertical is an older property that makes the same choice as text-orientation, and CSSMedia reads it as that property: auto is mixed, 0deg is upright and 90deg is sideways. Use text-orientation in new stylesheets.

With mixed, the Unicode property Vertical_Orientation of each character decides: characters marked upright stand upright, and the others are turned. A character with its accents or marks is one unit and turns as a whole, and a character inside an enclosing mark, such as a circle, stands upright.

Upright characters use the vertical metrics of the font and its vertical forms, so the Japanese stop, the brackets and the long vowel mark are drawn in the forms made for vertical lines. Arabic letters set upright take their isolated forms. Turned text keeps the horizontal widths, ligatures and forms of the font. CSSMedia shapes complex scripts such as Arabic, Hebrew, Thai and Devanagari as a line first, and then turns the result, so letters still join and marks stay in place in sideways text.

step.cmd: Put short numbers upright in one place

info.p: A number or a short code in a vertical line is often set side by side in the space of one character. text-combine-upright: all does it for the whole element, and digits does it for each run of digits that has no more digits than the number that follows, from 2 to 4:

With this rule, 12 in the text is one upright unit, the width of a character. 2026 has four digits, so it stays as it is. Digits that are split by the start or the end of an element are not combined when, together, they would be too long: with digits 4, the 12 and the 34 of 1234 stay as they are.

The combined text fits in a square of one em, centered on the line. Two characters take the half-width forms of the font when it has them. Longer text is compressed. Full-width digits are set as ordinary digits first. Spaces at the start and at the end of the element are dropped, and letter spacing and line feeds inside it are ignored. For emphasis marks the unit counts as one character and gets one mark.
The property works in all the vertical writing modes. In sideways-rl and sideways-lr the combined text stands upright in the turned line. It has no effect in horizontal-tb.

step.cmd: Set the direction of the text

info.p: The properties direction and unicode-bidi work along the line. With direction: rtl, a vertical line goes from the bottom to the top, and text of a script that is written from right to left, such as Arabic or Hebrew, is ordered as it is in horizontal text. A paragraph that mixes Japanese and Arabic orders its parts by the Unicode bidirectional algorithm, as horizontal text does. With text-orientation: upright, the direction is always ltr and every character counts as left to right, so an upright Hebrew or Arabic word reads from top to bottom in the order of its letters.

The physical properties keep their meaning: width is the horizontal size of a box on the page, whatever the writing mode. In a vertical element, the length of the line is its height. To write one stylesheet for both directions, use the logical properties inline-size, block-size, margin-block-start, margin-inline-end, padding-block-end, border-inline-start and the others of their family. They follow the writing mode, so the same rule spaces a paragraph in horizontal and in vertical text:

In vertical-rl, the block start is the right side, so the border is on the right of the paragraph and the space is on its left. The border, the padding and the margin of a box, its background, its list markers and its tables all follow this rule. A background image is placed by physical terms: background-position: top right is the top right corner of the box in every writing mode. The values left and right of float, of clear and of text-align are the two sides of the line: in a vertical line, left is the top and right is the bottom. inline-start and inline-end follow the direction of the text.

CSSMedia breaks vertical lines where horizontal ones are broken, with the rules of Chinese, Japanese and Korean text. A closing bracket, a comma or a stop does not start a line, an opening bracket does not end one, and a dash or an ellipsis of two characters is not split. line-break sets how strict the rules are:

ul.li: normal and strict keep small kana such as ゃ, the long vowel mark ー and the iteration marks such as 々 off the start of a line, and do not break between the dots of an ellipsis.
In Chinese and Japanese text, normal and loose let the wave dash 〜 and ゠ start a line, and strict does not. In other languages they never start a line.

info.p: Set the language of the document, as explains, so that the rules of the right language apply.
Japanese brackets, commas and stops are drawn in a full square, half of which is blank. text-spacing-trim says when that blank half is removed, so that the mark takes half a square:

ul.li: normal, the initial value, keeps an opening bracket at the start of a line full, removes the blank half of a closing mark at the end of a line only when that lets the line fit, and removes one blank between two marks that stand together, such as 」「 or 。」.
trim-start also makes an opening bracket half at the start of every line.
space-first makes it half at the start of a line, except on the first line of a paragraph and after a line feed.
trim-both makes opening brackets half at the start of lines and closing marks half at the end of lines.
trim-all makes every opening, closing and middle dot mark half, wherever it is.

info.p: An opening bracket loses the blank before it, on the left in horizontal text and at the top in vertical text, and a closing mark loses the blank after it. The glyph stays the same, and only its space changes. In Japanese text, the colon counts as a middle dot and the comma and the stop as closing marks. Marks of a font that draws them in their own narrow width, such as the quotation marks of a Latin font, keep that width.

Underlines, overlines and lines through the text are drawn along the line, on the sides of the characters. An underline of a vertical line is on its left, under the text, and an overline is on its right. text-underline-position chooses the place of the underline:

ul.li: auto puts it just under the alphabetic baseline, the line on which Latin letters stand.
from-font takes its place from the font.
under puts it under the whole text, below the lowest character.
left and right put it on that side of a vertical line, outside the characters. With right, the overline moves to the left. In horizontal text, left and right act as auto.

info.p: text-underline-offset moves the underline that far away from the text. When the line crosses characters of several sizes, the overline goes over the tallest of them and an underline with under below the lowest. Other underlines take the average place that the fonts and sizes give, below the lowest baseline. A line through the text is drawn through each size at its own height. Emphasis marks and shadows work in vertical text too. explains them.

step.cmd: Write the margin boxes in vertical lines

info.p: Each margin box of the page has its own writing mode. The boxes of the top and the bottom margin are wide and short, so text in them is usually horizontal, and the boxes of the side margins are tall and narrow, where vertical text fits. Set writing-mode in the margin box rule:

An element with a different writing mode from its parent is laid out in its own mode, as a box of its own, and then placed in the flow of its parent. Its margins are those of the parent's sides, so margin-left: auto and margin-right: auto center a vertical box in horizontal text, and its margins collapse with those of the boxes above and below it. An inline element with another writing mode becomes an inline block.
The lines of a vertical box inside horizontal text are as long as its height. Give it a height to choose that length:

Without a height, CSSMedia sizes the box for you. A short text that fits on one line makes the box as long as the text. A longer text is set in lines as long as the height of the parent when the parent has a fixed or maximum height, or else as long as the page area. The lines fill the width of the parent, and the text that does not fit goes on in a second band of lines below the first, as in columns. With column-count or column-width on the box, you choose the columns yourself. A float, an inline block or a table cell that holds such a box is as wide as the box. A table of the other writing mode takes the size of its content, and the text of a cell is broken into lines as long as the page area.

A MathML formula is always laid out horizontally, whatever the writing mode of the text around it. In a vertical line it takes its place as one box, upright, and the line makes room for it. Images are never turned: an image keeps its width and its height on the page, and so does the default size of 300px by 150px of an image that has no size of its own.

step.cmd: Use vertical text in a drawing

info.p: The text of an SVG drawing takes the same properties. explains how.

result.p: The text of your document is written in vertical lines, with the lines of the page and the boxes of the page following the writing mode.
